result.markdown: --- title: "Session 4 — Diagnostics, Derived Variables and the Number of Imputations" subtitle: "Fraction of missing information · how many imputations · passive imputation · interactions · auxiliary variables · Lab 4" author: "Community Medicine Workshop" format: revealjs: theme: serif css: [../assets/slide_deck.css, assets/workshop.css, assets/quiz.css] include-after-body: assets/quiz-include.html embed-resources: true slide-number: true navigation-mode: linear code-copy: true center: false transition: fade width: 1280 height: 720 fig-align: center html-math-method: plain execute: echo: true warning: false message: false fig-width: 9 fig-height: 4.6 fig-dpi: 100 --- ## Where we are ::: {.incremental} - Session 3: impute, analyse, pool - Today: the **details** that decide whether MI is done **well** - By the end you can: - read the **fraction of missing information** - choose the **number of imputations** - handle a **derived variable** and an **interaction** - use **auxiliary variables** ::: # Topic 1 — How much did the missing data cost? {background-color="#2C3E50"} ## Fraction of missing information ::: {.cell} ```{.r .cell-code} fit <- with(imp, lm(sbp ~ age + sex + bmi + smoker + activity)) pool(fit)$pooled[, c("term", "fmi", "lambda")] |> mutate(across(where(is.numeric), \(x) round(x, 2))) ``` ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-stdout} ``` term fmi lambda 1 (Intercept) 0.25 0.25 2 age 0.07 0.07 3 sexMale 0.12 0.11 4 bmi 0.26 0.26 5 smokerYes 0.24 0.23 6 activity 0.15 0.14 ``` ::: ::: ::: {.incremental} - **fmi** = the share of the **variance of the estimate** that is due to the missing data - BMI **0.26**, smoking **0.24**, activity **0.15**; age **0.07** (complete: only the sampling noise of the imputation) - It is **not** the percentage of missing values; it also reflects how well the other variables **predict** the missing ones - A high fmi means **more imputations** are needed ::: ## How many imputations? ::: {.cell} ```{.r .cell-code} se_bmi <- function(m, seed) { i <- mice(dat2, m = m, maxit = 10, seed = seed, printFlag = FALSE); s <- summary(pool(with(i, lm(sbp ~ age + sex + bmi + smoker + activity)))); s$std.error[s$term == "bmi"] } sapply(c(m5 = 5, m50 = 50), function(m) round(range(sapply(1:6, function(seed) se_bmi(m, seed))), 3)) ``` ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-stdout} ``` m5 m50 [1,] 0.063 0.065 [2,] 0.089 0.071 ``` ::: ::: ::: {.key} Six different seeds: with **m = 5** the pooled SE of BMI ranges from **0.063 to 0.089**; with **m = 50**, only **0.065 to 0.071**. More imputations make the results **independent of the seed**. Old advice (m = 5) is **outdated**: use **at least as many as the percentage of incomplete cases** (here 55), at least 20. ::: # Topic 2 — Analysis complications {background-color="#2C3E50"} ## A derived variable: hypertension ::: {.cell} ```{.r .cell-code} long <- complete(imp, "long", include = TRUE) |> mutate(htn = as.integer(sbp >= 140)) imp_h <- as.mids(long) fit_h <- with(imp_h, glm(htn ~ age + sex + bmi + smoker, family = binomial)) summary(pool(fit_h), conf.int = TRUE, exponentiate = TRUE)[-1, c("term", "estimate", "2.5 %", "97.5 %")] |> mutate(across(where(is.numeric), \(x) round(x, 2))) ``` ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-stdout} ``` term estimate 2.5 % 97.5 % 2 age 1.07 1.06 1.08 3 sexMale 1.54 1.13 2.10 4 bmi 1.14 1.09 1.19 5 smokerYes 1.47 1.02 2.10 ``` ::: ::: ::: {.incremental} - **Impute the original variable (SBP)**, then **derive** hypertension **inside each data set** ("passive" imputation) - **Never** dichotomise **before** imputing: you would throw away information and make the imputation model **less accurate** - Odds ratio **1.14 per BMI unit** (95% CI 1.09 to 1.19) ::: ## An interaction ::: {.cell} ```{.r .cell-code} fit_full <- with(imp, lm(sbp ~ age + sex * bmi + smoker + activity)) fit_red <- with(imp, lm(sbp ~ age + sex + bmi + smoker + activity)) D1(fit_full, fit_red) ``` ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-stdout} ``` test statistic df1 df2 dfcom p.value riv 1 ~~ 2 0.48808 1 474.1462 1993 0.4851275 0.164633 ``` ::: ::: ::: {.incremental} - `D1()`: **pooled Wald test** of the extra term across the imputed data sets (p = 0.49: no sex difference) - If you plan an **interaction** or a **curve**, the **imputation model must contain it** (e.g. impute **separately by group**, or add the product as a variable), otherwise the imputed values behave **as if no interaction existed**, biasing it **towards zero** ::: ## Auxiliary variables ::: {.cell} ```{.r .cell-code} imp_no <- mice(dat2 |> select(-hba1c), m = 20, maxit = 10, seed = 2038, printFlag = FALSE) b_no <- summary(pool(with(imp_no, lm(sbp ~ age + sex + bmi + smoker + activity)))) b_full <- summary(pool(fit)) round(c(without_hba1c = b_no$estimate[b_no$term == "bmi"], with_hba1c = b_full$estimate[b_full$term == "bmi"]), 3) ``` ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-stdout} ``` without_hba1c with_hba1c 0.799 0.790 ``` ::: ::: ::: {.key} **HbA1c is not in the SBP model**, but it is **related to BMI** and to the missingness. Including it as an **auxiliary variable** costs nothing and can **reduce bias and increase precision**; here the effect is **small** (0.80 vs 0.79). Include variables that **predict the missing values or the missingness**. ::: ## Checklist ::: {.good} 1. Report the **fmi** for key estimates 2. **m** large enough that results do not depend on the **seed** 3. **Derive** variables after imputing; keep **interactions** and **curves** in the imputation model 4. Add **auxiliary** variables 5. Use **`D1()`/`D3()`** for tests of several coefficients, not the average of p-values ::: ## 🔧 Switch to R — Lab 4 {.lab-slide background-color="#1565c0"} ::: {.lab-box} **File:** `missing-workshop/labs/lab4_diagnostics.R` - fmi, and the number of imputations - hypertension derived after imputing - an interaction with `D1`, auxiliary variables ::: **Time:** 40 minutes · answer the Q questions in the comments ## Self-check quiz (1/5) {.smaller} ::: {.quiz-q data-qid="m4q1" data-type="mcq" data-hash="w5x9sr.4lrn4y" data-show="QWJvdXQgMzAlIG9mIHRoZSB2YXJpYW5jZSBvZiB0aGUgZXN0aW1hdGUgaXMgZHVlIHRvIHRo ZSBtaXNzaW5nIGRhdGE=" data-explain="VGhlIGZyYWN0aW9uIG9mIG1pc3NpbmcgaW5mb3JtYXRpb24gaXMgdGhlIHNoYXJlIG9mIHRo ZSB0b3RhbCB2YXJpYW5jZSBhdHRyaWJ1dGFibGUgdG8gdGhlIG1pc3NpbmcgZGF0YS4gSXQg aXMgbm90IHRoZSBwZXJjZW50YWdlIG9mIG1pc3NpbmcgdmFsdWVzLg=="} A pooled estimate has an fmi of 0.3. What does that mean? - About 30% of the variance of the estimate is due to the missing data - 30% of the values of the variable were found to be missing in the dataset - The estimate is 30% biased because of the missing data in the dataset - 30% of the imputed data sets gave a different answer from the others ::: ## Self-check quiz (2/5) {.smaller} ::: {.quiz-q data-qid="m4q2" data-type="mcq" data-hash="w5xn1i.4ls1md" data-show="VGhlIHJlc3VsdHMsIGFuZCB0aGUgU0VzIGluIHBhcnRpY3VsYXIsIGRlcGVuZCBtdWNoIGxl c3Mgb24gdGhlIHNlZWQ=" data-explain="V2l0aCBmZXcgaW1wdXRhdGlvbnMgdGhlIGJldHdlZW4taW1wdXRhdGlvbiB2YXJpYW5jZSBp cyBwb29ybHkgZXN0aW1hdGVkLCBzbyBTRXMgY2hhbmdlIGZyb20gb25lIHNlZWQgdG8gYW5v dGhlci4gTW9yZSBpbXB1dGF0aW9ucyBzdGFiaWxpc2UgdGhlbS4="} Why use m = 50 rather than m = 5 for the final analysis? - More imputations remove the bias that comes from data missing not at random - m = 5 cannot be combined with Rubin's rules, which need at least ten sets - The results, and the SEs in particular, depend much less on the seed - The estimates become more extreme as m is increased from 5 to 50 sets ::: ## Self-check quiz (3/5) {.smaller} ::: {.quiz-q data-qid="m4q3" data-type="mcq" data-hash="w5y0a6.4lsg3p" data-show="SW1wdXRlIFNCUCwgdGhlbiBkZXJpdmUgaHlwZXJ0ZW5zaW9uIGluIGVhY2ggY29tcGxldGVk IGRhdGEgc2V0" data-explain="RGVyaXZlZCB2YXJpYWJsZXMgYXJlIGNvbXB1dGVkIGFmdGVyIGltcHV0YXRpb24gd2l0aGlu IGVhY2ggZGF0YSBzZXQsIHNvIHRoZXkgc3RheSBjb25zaXN0ZW50IHdpdGggdGhlIGltcHV0 ZWQgb3JpZ2luYWwgdmFyaWFibGUgYW5kIG5vIGluZm9ybWF0aW9uIGlzIGxvc3Qu"} SBP is incomplete and the analysis needs hypertension (SBP of 140 or more). Which is the right order? - Derive hypertension first and impute the 0/1 variable as it stands - Impute SBP, then derive hypertension in each completed data set - Impute both variables separately so that they are independent - Derive it from the average of the 20 imputed SBP values for each adult ::: ## Self-check quiz (4/5) {.smaller} ::: {.quiz-q data-qid="m4q4" data-type="mcq" data-hash="w5ydiw.4lsul3" data-show="T3RoZXJ3aXNlIHRoZSBpbXB1dGVkIGRhdGEgaG9sZCBubyBpbnRlcmFjdGlvbiwgd2hpY2gg Ymlhc2VzIGl0IHRvIHplcm8=" data-explain="VGhlIGltcHV0YXRpb24gbW9kZWwgc2hvdWxkIGJlIGF0IGxlYXN0IGFzIHJpY2ggYXMgdGhl IGFuYWx5c2lzIG1vZGVsLiBJZiBpdCBpZ25vcmVzIHRoZSBpbnRlcmFjdGlvbiwgdGhlIGlt cHV0ZWQgZGF0YSBjb250YWluIG5vbmUsIGFuZCB0aGUgcG9vbGVkIGFuYWx5c2lzIHVuZGVy ZXN0aW1hdGVzIGl0Lg=="} Why should the imputation model contain the interaction you plan to test? - The software refuses to pool a model whose terms were not all imputed together - Interactions are estimated correctly after the data are standardised first - Otherwise the imputed data hold no interaction, which biases it to zero - Interaction terms are the variables that most need imputation in a dataset ::: ## Self-check quiz (5/5) {.smaller} ::: {.quiz-q data-qid="m4q5" data-type="mcq" data-hash="w5yqrm.4lt92h" data-show="UHJlZGljdG9ycyBvZiB0aGUgbWlzc2luZyB2YWx1ZXMgb3Igb2YgbWlzc2luZ25lc3MsIGtl cHQgb3V0IG9mIHRoZSBhbmFseXNpcw==" data-explain="QXV4aWxpYXJ5IHZhcmlhYmxlcyBhcmUgaW4gdGhlIGltcHV0YXRpb24gbW9kZWwgb25seS4g VGhleSBjYXJyeSBpbmZvcm1hdGlvbiBhYm91dCB0aGUgbWlzc2luZyB2YWx1ZXMgb3IgdGhl IG1pc3NpbmduZXNzIGFuZCBjYW4gcmVkdWNlIGJpYXMgYW5kIGluY3JlYXNlIHByZWNpc2lv bi4="} What are auxiliary variables in multiple imputation? - Variables that have to appear in the analysis model as well, or results are invalid - Variables with no missing values, which are used to check the imputations afterwards - Variables that replace the outcome in the imputation model to avoid circularity - Predictors of the missing values or of missingness, kept out of the analysis ::: ## Score and take-home **Your score: ** ::: {.incremental} - **fmi**: share of variance due to missing data - **m ≥ percent of incomplete cases** (and ≥ 20); fix a seed - **Impute, then derive**; never dichotomise first - Put **interactions and curves** into the imputation model - **Auxiliary variables** help; test several coefficients with `D1()` ::: **Next:** Session 5: sensitivity analysis for MNAR and reporting

<script>
  // htmlwidgets need to know to resize themselves when slides are shown/hidden.
  // Fire the "slideenter" event (handled by htmlwidgets.js) when the current
  // slide changes (different for each slide format).
  (function () {
    // dispatch for htmlwidgets
    function fireSlideEnter() {
      const event = window.document.createEvent("Event");
      event.initEvent("slideenter", true, true);
      window.document.dispatchEvent(event);
    }

    function fireSlideChanged(previousSlide, currentSlide) {
      fireSlideEnter();

      // dispatch for shiny
      if (window.jQuery) {
        if (previousSlide) {
          window.jQuery(previousSlide).trigger("hidden");
        }
        if (currentSlide) {
          window.jQuery(currentSlide).trigger("shown");
        }
      }
    }

    // hookup for slidy
    if (window.w3c_slidy) {
      window.w3c_slidy.add_observer(function (slide_num) {
        // slide_num starts at position 1
        fireSlideChanged(null, w3c_slidy.slides[slide_num - 1]);
      });
    }

  })();
</script>
